blockDescriptions.block_01: C++ Foundations & Object-Oriented Design — references, arrays, classes, inheritance, templates, exceptions
blockDescriptions.block_02: Arrays, Linked Lists & Recursion — linked list implementation, recursion, asymptotic (Big-O) analysis
blockDescriptions.block_03: Stacks, Queues & Sequence-Based Structures — stacks, queues/deques, vectors, iterators, bubble sort
blockDescriptions.block_04: Trees & Tree Traversal — general trees, traversal algorithms, binary trees
blockDescriptions.block_06: Maps, Hash Tables & Dictionaries — hash functions, skip lists, ordered maps
blockDescriptions.block_07: Balanced & Search Trees — BST, AVL, multi-way search, (2,4)/red-black trees
blockDescriptions.block_08: Sorting Algorithms & Course Capstone — merge sort, selection sort, cumulative review

requiredCourseModel.tierQuestionFocus: Prior exposure to C++ specifically (not just general programming from CS-UH 1001)

personalizationRules: This is a REQUIRED, cumulative course — every enrolled student is examined on the entire syllabus. Every block MUST appear in every pathway. NEVER omit a block, and never drop a block's node count to zero, regardless of the student's background.

Every node MUST include syllabusBlockId set to exactly one block id from the catalog, and MUST include nodeRole (one of: core_required, scaffolding_catchup, enrichment_advanced, assessment) and a one-sentence personalizationRationale.

Personalization here means a FIXED DESTINATION with a PERSONALIZED ROUTE: the goal is to help a student with less prior exposure to C++ specifically (even if they know general programming from CS-UH 1001) catch up to their classmates FASTER, not to teach them less or teach them longer overall.

If the student reports little or no prior C++ exposure (no_prior_exposure tier — e.g. only Python/Java before this course): add extra nodes tagged scaffolding_catchup concentrated in block_01 (C++ Foundations & OOD), since pointers, references, and manual memory semantics are the main friction point for the rest of the course.

If the student reports some prior C++ exposure (some_prior_exposure tier): include a moderate number of scaffolding_catchup nodes in block_01 — fewer than the no-prior-exposure case, more than the strong-exposure case.

If the student reports strong prior C++ exposure (strong_prior_exposure tier, e.g. has already written non-trivial C++ programs): keep block_01 to its floor-level core_required nodes only, and instead add enrichment_advanced nodes (move semantics, template metaprogramming, RAII idioms) — reinvest the freed-up capacity, do not shorten the pathway.

block_07 (Balanced & Search Trees) is the most proof/theory-heavy block. Students who report low comfort with discrete-math/proof-style reasoning may also get 1-2 extra scaffolding_catchup nodes there, in addition to whatever their C++ tier assigns in block_01 — this is a secondary, smaller signal, not the primary axis.

The TOTAL number of nodes must stay within the target node band (see requiredCourseModel.targetNodeBand) for every profile regardless of tier. Personalization must show up as a shift in the MIX of scaffolding_catchup vs. enrichment_advanced nodes, not as a longer or shorter pathway.

Every node's wording (description) may reflect the student's stated interests or goals (e.g., framing hash tables with a 'how Python dicts work' analogy vs. a 'how database indexes work' analogy), but this must NEVER change which blocks appear, how many nodes per block, or the presence of required content.
Every pathway must include at least one assessment-type node tied to the midterm-review material (in or after block_03) and one tied to the cumulative final-review material (in block_08).
